description: Apply a deterministic feasibility‑preserving simulated‑annealing refinement to a seed layout before a final gradient‑based optimisation.

guidance.idea: Starting from a deterministic seed (e.g., a hexagonal lattice), run a simulated‑annealing loop that only accepts moves which keep the layout feasible (no overlaps, inside bounds). Use a deterministic pseudo‑random generator so the whole process is reproducible. After annealing, compute the exact uniform size via the LP step and finish with a short SLSQP polish.
guidance.transfer_rule: Useful for any layout or packing problem where feasibility can be checked quickly and a deterministic annealing schedule is desired.
actions: Seed the layout with a simple deterministic pattern.
Generate a candidate move (e.g., perturb a centre).
Reject the move if it violates feasibility.
Accept the move according to a deterministic temperature schedule.
After annealing, compute the optimal uniform size (e.g., via LP).
Run a brief SLSQP refinement on the positions.
cautions: The annealing temperature schedule must be deterministic to keep the pipeline reproducible.
Only feasibility‑preserving moves are allowed; this may limit exploration if the schedule is too aggressive.
Ensure the final SLSQP step respects the time budget.
